wizard.why.alerts: If the roof can't close or the mount won't park, an alert is how you'll find out. Tick as many channels as you like.
wizard.why.board: The board decides which pins drive the motor. Nothing is driven until one is chosen and the device restarts.
wizard.why.calibrate: A slow, attended open and close measures the travel time and the Hall readings, and proposes the settings.
wizard.why.daylight: Sunlight through the telescope can damage the camera. Some owners image the sun, so this is your call.
wizard.why.direction: A first short move, with you watching: a motor wired the wrong way round would drive the roof into its end stop.
wizard.why.done: The commissioning guide's dry runs and its gate for unattended use come next, with someone at the roof.
wizard.why.leave: Saved answers stay saved. Until setup is finished or skipped, the dashboard offers to carry on.
wizard.why.motion: For a roof without its motor yet. Travel and speed set each move's time limit; the calibration run measures them later.
wizard.why.name: N.I.N.A. and Home Assistant show this name, so pick one you'll recognise among your devices.
wizard.why.network: On a board with Ethernet WiFi is optional. Auto uses Ethernet and falls back to saved WiFi.
wizard.why.nina: Before closing, the roof asks N.I.N.A. to park the mount and checks the park. Without it, the roof can't close itself.
wizard.why.parkSwitchCount: Every fitted switch must read closed. Two on separate cables catch a short or a stuck switch.
wizard.why.parkSwitches: The roof closes only onto a parked mount. Switches alone need no N.I.N.A., but a stuck one can't be seen.
wizard.why.password: Anyone who can reach the device can change its settings and move the roof. A password keeps that to you.
wizard.why.review: Each check reads the device as it is now. Change opens the part of setup that sets it.
wizard.why.site: The daylight check works out the sun's altitude from the site, and alerts and the move log use the device's clock.
wizard.why.sqmeter: RoofRoof reads the weather verdict from SQMeter and can follow its location and copy its time zone, MQTT and alert settings.
wizard.why.teach: Move the roof slowly to each end and mark it; the device sets the Hall thresholds from what it reads there.
wizard.why.testBox: On a test box with no telescope and no weather station yet, the park and weather checks would refuse every move. Test box mode bypasses them for a while; faults are always checked.
wizard.why.wiring: It reads each input and the EN pull-down without moving the roof, so a wiring mistake shows before the first move.
wizard.wiring.later: You can skip this and check the wiring later on the pins page.
